extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of literary/personal essays (students of literature, general readers of Montaigne)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit stylistic standards for composing personal, digressive essays — emphasizing candidness, readable prose, measured digression, and poetic vigor within prose. Suited to reflective, autobiographical/meditative essay-writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fullness and candidness in memoir/essay
rubrics_metrics.description: I have either told or designed to tell all; what I cannot express, I point out with my finger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for openness and completeness about the self in memoir/essay. If some feelings or facts cannot be expressed, flag or indicate them rather than conceal them; do not leave critical gaps that require readers to guess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affected obscurity (no false profundity)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some humours in which comprehension produces disdain; who will think better of me for not understanding what I say, and will conclude the depth of my sense by its obscurity; which, to speak in good sooth, I mortally hate, and would avoid it if I could.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not deliberately obscure meaning in order to seem deep. Clarity is a virtue; avoid stylistic affectations that make text needlessly opaque. Authentic subtlety should not rely on baffling the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let the matter itself show structure (avoid gratuitous connectors)
rubrics_metrics.description: I would have my matter distinguish itself; it sufficiently shows where it changes, where it concludes, where it begins, and where it rejoins, without interlacing it with words of connection introduced for the relief of weak or negligent ears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange content so that transitions and structure are evident from the material itself. Minimize forced connective phrases used merely to guide inattentive readers; trust the reader and the text’s internal markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use digression and 'poetic progress' by leaps and skips
rubrics_metrics.description: I love a poetic progress, by leaps and skips; 'tis an art, as Plato says, light, nimble, demoniac. ... how beautiful are these frolicsome sallies, those variations and digressions, and all the more when they seem most fortuitous and careless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit and cultivate digression, playful sallies, and non-linear progression in essays. Leaps and unexpected turns can be an artistic device; allow apparent carelessness when it yields lively, interesting movement of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sections long enough to require leisure
rubrics_metrics.description: The frequent breaks into chapters that I made my method in the beginning of my book, having since seemed to me to dissolve the attention before it was raised, ... I have made them longer, such as require proposition and assigned leisure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive fragmentation that prevents readers from engaging deeply. Structure chapters/sections so they contain a proposition and allow sustained attention; prefer fewer, more substantial sections over many tiny ones that dissipate focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not write for cursory consumption — require reader's time
rubrics_metrics.description: In such an employment, to whom you will not give an hour you give nothing; and you do nothing for him for whom you only do it whilst you are doing something else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that certain essays presuppose focused reading. If the subject requires contemplation, write with the expectation that readers will give it time; do not aim primarily for ephemeral or merely skimmable impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend poetic vigour into prose
rubrics_metrics.description: The best old prose ... shines throughout with the lustre, vigour, and boldness of poetry, and not without some air of its fury. And certainly prose ought to have the pre-eminence in speaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In prose writing, allow rhetorical boldness and lyrical energy usually associated with poetry. Prose should command attention and can incorporate poetic qualities while remaining fundamentally prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles can be marks, not exhaustive summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The titles of my chapters do not always comprehend the whole matter; they often denote it by some mark only, as these others, Andria, Eunuchus; or these, Sylla, Cicero, Toyquatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titles as signposts or evocative markers rather than exhaustive descriptions. Accept that a title may indicate a theme or motif without capturing every direction the section will take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer natural inclination over strict doctrinal precepts
rubrics_metrics.description: I make it my business to bring vanity itself in repute, and folly too, if it produce me any pleasure; and let myself follow my own natural inclinations, without carrying too strict a hand upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow personal temperament and spontaneous pleasure to shape the essay. Do not over-constrain oneself to rigid moral or stylistic rules at the expense of genuine expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal when you speak of yourself with consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: At the worst, this difform liberty of presenting ourselves two several ways, the actions after one manner and the reasoning after another, may be allowed to those who only speak of things; but it cannot be allowed to those who speak of themselves, as I do: I must march my pen as I do my feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing autobiographically or confessional pieces, strive for consistency between described actions and stated reasoning. Personal writing invites coherence between life and narration; avoid open contradictions without acknowledging them.
